newsitem.title: DUBAI: Many illegal residents defied UAE amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Many illegal residents defied UAE amnesty.

text.p: More than 167,000 illegal workers have left the United Arab Emirates under a three-month amnesty, but many remain in the Gulf Arab state, a senior government official was on Wednesday quoted as saying.

"As many as 167,750 illegal immigrants had left the UAE by October 31, but many more illegals are still in the country," Interior Minister Lieutenant-General Mohammad Said al-Badi said in comments published in al-Bayan newspaper.
"They (the violators) will be held liable for their action. The authorities are determined to execute the law strictly," al-Badi added.

Foreign workers, mainly from the Indian subcontinent and southeast Asia -- make up 75 to 80 percent of the 2.4 million-strong population. The Illegal workers have flooded out of the oil-rich state to avoid penalties such as jail terms, fines and deportation under tough new labour laws.

Many foreign workers come to the UAE legally, but break the law by staying on when their visas expire or by absconding from their sponsors. The practices have always been illegal, but the new law imposes tougher penalties.
Diplomats had estimated that 200,000 illegal workers would leave the UAE by the end of the amnesty on October 31.
